correctness.rationale: The monotone restriction to a persistent cycle is an increasing bijection of a finite chain and fixes it pointwise, so fixed points are precisely the obstruction to nilpotence even without injectivity. Marking fixed points forces monotone values into the adjacent closed target intervals; the end gaps therefore give B, the interior gaps C, and no marked point gives A. Signed marking gives A−zu B²/(1+zu C). Summing the coefficient identity [x^m]T(x)^(m+h)/(1−x) by substituting x=zT(x) gives the Jacobian denominator (1−zR)(1−zT′(zR))=R sqrt(Δ), yielding exactly the stated radical and constant term 1. For uniform singularity, R=2/(1+z+sqrt(Δ)) is nonzero on the chosen branch near the dominant disk. A zero of sqrt(Δ)+uzR would require sqrt(Δ)=−u(1+z)/(u+2), hence (1+z)^2=(u+2)^2 z. At u=1 the smaller root (7−3√5)/2 is positive and has the opposite sign of sqrt(Δ); the larger is outside a slit disk containing the dominant singularity. These exclusions persist in a common rescaled slit neighborhood after z=ρ(u)w for complex u near 1. The denominator at z=ρ equals u/(1+u) and the linear coefficient in sqrt(Δ) of its reciprocal is −sqrt(1+u)/(u²sqrt(ρ)); the expansion is a convergent Puiseux series, so uniform transfer gives the stated relative O(1/n). The leading log-mgf is 2n arsinh(sqrt(exp(t))) up to its value at t=0, giving derivatives 1/√2 and 1/(4√2) after division by n. Uniform analytic error permits differentiation for the O(1) moment remainders and gives the centered normalized Gaussian law.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration only corroborates the formal coefficients; the complex-uniform transfer and limit law are justified by the singularity argument.
